name: Ghana
summary_text: Ghana is dangerous for trans visitors — and narrowly avoided becoming much worse. In February 2024 parliament unanimously passed the Human Sexual Rights and Family Values Bill: up to 3 years in prison for simply identifying as LGBT, and 5 years for “promotion.” President Akufo-Addo refused to assent pending legal challenges, the Supreme Court dismissed the challenges in December 2024, and the bill lapsed when the 8th parliament dissolved — but its unanimous passage and broad public support signal the political climate, and reintroduction is expected. Under existing law, “unnatural carnal knowledge” carries up to 3 years, and mob justice against perceived LGBT people is documented. There is no legal gender recognition and no anti-discrimination protection. Accra has a resilient underground community (LGBT+ Rights Ghana — whose 2021 office opening was raided and shut down within weeks), but nothing that can protect a visitor.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying Reuters report (Feb 2024) covers Ghana's parliament passing the anti-LGBT bill.

sources.title: Ghana: President Should Veto Anti-LGBT Bill | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Mar 2024): 'Ghana: President Should Veto Anti-LGBT Bill' — urges a veto of the bill sharply increasing penalties and criminalising advocacy.

sources.title: Ghana anti-LGBT bill: Supreme Court dismisses legal challenges
sources.claim_summary: BBC (Dec 2024): Ghana's Supreme Court unanimously dismissed two legal challenges to the anti-LGBT bill (three years' imprisonment for identifying as LGBT, five for forming or funding LGBT groups), ruling the cases could not be reviewed until presidential assent. Gay sex was already punishable by up to three years. Fear and uncertainty gripped Ghana's LGBT community; the UN condemned the bill as one of Africa's most draconian.

sources.title: Ghana passes law criminalising identifying as LGBTQ+ - JURIST - News
sources.claim_summary: JURIST (Feb 2024): Ghana's Parliament unanimously passed the Promotion of Proper Human Sexual Rights and Ghanaian Family Values Bill 2021, criminalising identifying as LGBTQ+ (up to 3 years) and forming or funding LGBT groups (up to 5 years); the bill proscribes 'propaganda, advocacy or promotion' of LGBTQ+ activities.

HRW report (Jan 2018) 'No Choice but to Deny Who I Am': full PDF - violence and discrimination against LGBT people in Ghana; section 104(1)(b) criminalises 'unnatural carnal knowledge' but is rarely enforced; documents mob violence, police abuse, and extortion.

sources.title: “No Choice but to Deny Who I Am”: Violence and Discrimination against LGBT People in Ghana | HRW
sources.claim_summary: HRW report page (Jan 2018): opens with Pearl's account - a lesbian woman beaten by a crowd and nearly burned in Kumasi after a police officer kicked her; Ghana criminalises same-sex conduct via a colonial-era law that is rarely enforced, but unlike some neighbours has not stiffened penalties - documents pervasive violence and discrimination.

Bachelor thesis (Diaconia University of Applied Sciences, Helsinki, 2017) by Seree Yeboa-Mensa: survey of 113 Ghanaians living in Finland on LGBT rights in Ghana - most opposed decriminalisation/legalisation, citing religio-cultural reasons and effects on children; most supported families loving and accepting LGBT members but not blessing their marriages.
